html:
The Demak Sultanate was the first Muslim state on Java, a port kingdom on the island's north coast founded in the late 15th century. In about a century it overcame Majapahit and helped make Islam the main religion of Java.

Demak began as a port under Hindu-Buddhist Majapahit. Muslim traders from China, Gujarat, Arabia, Champa, Pasai and Malacca brought Islam to the north coast towns, which grew rich on the rice and spice trade. Its first ruler, Raden Patah, is said in Javanese tradition to have been a son of the last Majapahit king and a Chinese mother.

What it did:

  • Its armies defeated Majapahit around 1527 and took over much of the north coast of Java and parts of southern Sumatra.
  • Under Raden Patah's son, Pati Unus, it sent a fleet against Portuguese Malacca in 1513, without success.
  • It built the Great Mosque of Demak, one of the oldest mosques in Indonesia, in Javanese style with a tiered roof rather than a dome.

Javanese tradition links Demak to the Wali Songo, nine saints who spread Islam using local arts such as the shadow puppet theatre, which helps explain why Javanese Islam kept so much of the older culture.

Demak fell apart in a succession war in the 1540s and 1550s, and power passed to Pajang and then to the inland Sultanate of Mataram at the end of the 16th century. Its role as the first Muslim state on Java made it central to the story of Islam in Indonesia.
sum: The Demak Sultanate was the first Muslim state on Java, a port kingdom on the island's north coast founded in the late 15th century. In about a century it overcame Majapahit and helped make Islam the main religion of Java.
